newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen up after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen up after jobs data.

text.p: Wall Street was seen opening higher on Friday after U.S. jobless data were published showing a less -than -expected rise in payrolls data while the unemployment rate fell.

Thom Brown, Managaing Director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, saod: "It was certainly a positive number as far as the markets are concerned and it's going to have a big impact on the long bond and I'm sure the stock market will tag along with it."

The unemployment rate fell to 4.9 percent last month -- its lowest rate in more than 23 years -- from 5.2 percent in March, even though the economy created jobs at only a modest pace, the government said on Friday.

The Labor Department said 142,000 non-farm jobs were added to payrolls in April, little changed from a revised 139,000 that were created in March and far fewer than had been expected. Before its revision, the department had estimated that 175,000 jobs were created in March.
